interaction.human_task_context: You are the wearer and only the Assistant's physical executor, not a second planner. Once the interaction starts, perform no action unless the Assistant's current instruction explicitly requests it; on an idle turn, leave the action empty and ask what to do next. Follow only the currently actionable, single-object step and do exactly what the Assistant says, without choosing, correcting, improving, reordering, or extending its plan. If the current instruction explicitly covers several objects, continue only those named jobs one object per response while that instruction remains active. The motor-object legend, simulator command keys, known-location text, and automatic navigation are grounding aids only; never use them to infer an answer, object location, route, source, or destination that the Assistant did not state. You may directly target a movable only when it is in your current view, it was established by a dedicated earlier inspection, or the Assistant explicitly states its concrete current source location. Its name, command key, or legend entry alone does not qualify, and an incorrect location does not qualify. Otherwise leave the action empty, ask the Assistant where it is, and follow only the room, landmark, navigation, or inspection step the Assistant explicitly gives; never use [Walk], [LookAt], or [Grab] on an unseen object as an automatic-navigation shortcut. Do not name or describe inspected contents, visible labels, locations, categories, or other camera evidence to the Assistant; the Assistant must reason from the video itself. After the current instruction is fully complete, use only a neutral acknowledgement that reveals no observed result, then wait for the next instruction. Never infer completion from score or world state and never end the episode yourself; only the Assistant's dedicated completion token or the action limit ends it.

invention.author_prose:
In the hotel suite bedroom, the low-vision wearer says, “I’m setting this desk up as a small snack-and-paperwork spot before visitors arrive. Please guide me; I can’t reliably tell which loose things here are relevant.”

The assistant first does not guess from the request alone. It asks the wearer to slowly scan the desk and the nearby shelf, then to look directly at the metal tongs so the camera can read the paper band around them. The view shows a folder lying on the desk, and on the bedroom shelf a bottle of water, an unpackaged bap, and tongs with a short visible “CLEAN” band. The assistant explains the domain rule separately from the visual facts: because the bap is ready-to-eat and will be offered to visitors, a clean serving utensil should be set out with it rather than leaving people to handle the bread by hand. The label matters only to confirm these are suitable tongs; the rule itself is not printed anywhere in the room.

The first instruction is to clear the workspace: move the folder from the desk onto the bedroom shelf so papers are available but not mixed into the snack area. After the wearer does that, the assistant confirms from the new view that the folder is now on the shelf and gives the next step: put the bottle of water on the desk as the drink item, leaving space for the food and utensil. When the bottle is placed, the assistant checks the desk again and says to bring the clean tongs over before moving the bap, because the utensil needs to be present at the serving spot. Once the tongs are on the desk, the assistant gives the final placement: put the bap on the desk beside the tongs, then stop rather than carrying the folder back or putting the tongs away.

A weak guide treats the task as ordinary tidying: it moves the folder to the shelf and the water and bap to the desk, but leaves the tongs on the shelf because the wearer did not explicitly ask for them. The strong guide succeeds by applying the accepted food-serving rule to the observed clean tongs and unpackaged bread. The scored successful state has the folder on the bedroom shelf, the bottle of water on the desk, the bap on the desk, and the clean tongs also on the desk.

capability.boundary: Nothing in the scene should state the decisive rule. Avoid speculative professional advice and do not make label reading the main challenge.
capability.few_shot: During a household clean-up, an adult has chlorine bleach, an acidic toilet cleaner, and ordinary glass cleaner on a utility counter. They ask for help staging supplies before cleaning. The assistant knows that chlorine bleach and acidic cleaner must never be mixed or used together on the same surface. It directs the wearer to place the toilet cleaner in the bathroom caddy, the bleach in a separate floor-cleaning caddy, and the glass cleaner with the window cloths, while explicitly preventing the proposed combined bucket. The final separate containment relations are scoreable without simulating a chemical reaction. A weak guide groups all cleaners into one bucket because they share a purpose.
capability.target: Supply a conservative domain rule the untrained wearer does not know and turn it into safe, concrete next steps.

invention.author_prose:
In the hotel suite bedroom, the low-vision wearer says, “I’m setting this desk up as a small snack-and-paperwork spot before visitors arrive. Please guide me; I can’t reliably tell which loose things here are relevant.”

The assistant first does not guess from the request alone. It asks the wearer to slowly scan the desk and the nearby shelf, then to look directly at the metal tongs so the camera can read the paper band around them. The view shows a folder lying on the desk, and on the bedroom shelf a bottle of water, an unpackaged bap, and tongs with a short visible “CLEAN” band. The assistant explains the domain rule separately from the visual facts: because the bap is ready-to-eat and will be offered to visitors, a clean serving utensil should be set out with it rather than leaving people to handle the bread by hand. The label matters only to confirm these are suitable tongs; the rule itself is not printed anywhere in the room.

The first instruction is to clear the workspace: move the folder from the desk onto the bedroom shelf so papers are available but not mixed into the snack area. After the wearer does that, the assistant confirms from the new view that the folder is now on the shelf and gives the next step: put the bottle of water on the desk as the drink item, leaving space for the food and utensil. When the bottle is placed, the assistant checks the desk again and says to bring the clean tongs over before moving the bap, because the utensil needs to be present at the serving spot. Once the tongs are on the desk, the assistant gives the final placement: put the bap on the desk beside the tongs, then stop rather than carrying the folder back or putting the tongs away.

A weak guide treats the task as ordinary tidying: it moves the folder to the shelf and the water and bap to the desk, but leaves the tongs on the shelf because the wearer did not explicitly ask for them. The strong guide succeeds by applying the accepted food-serving rule to the observed clean tongs and unpackaged bread. The scored successful state has the folder on the bedroom shelf, the bottle of water on the desk, the bap on the desk, and the clean tongs also on the desk.

capability.boundary: Nothing in the scene should state the decisive rule. Avoid speculative professional advice and do not make label reading the main challenge.
capability.few_shot: During a household clean-up, an adult has chlorine bleach, an acidic toilet cleaner, and ordinary glass cleaner on a utility counter. They ask for help staging supplies before cleaning. The assistant knows that chlorine bleach and acidic cleaner must never be mixed or used together on the same surface. It directs the wearer to place the toilet cleaner in the bathroom caddy, the bleach in a separate floor-cleaning caddy, and the glass cleaner with the window cloths, while explicitly preventing the proposed combined bucket. The final separate containment relations are scoreable without simulating a chemical reaction. A weak guide groups all cleaners into one bucket because they share a purpose.
capability.target: Supply a conservative domain rule the untrained wearer does not know and turn it into safe, concrete next steps.

cast.restaged_story: In bedroom_0 of hotel_suite_large, a low-vision wearer says, 'I'm setting this desk up as a small snack-and-paperwork spot before visitors arrive. Please guide me; I can't reliably tell which loose things here are relevant.' A folder lies on the desk; a bottle of water, an unpackaged bap, and tongs with a short 'CLEAN' band rest on the bedroom shelf. The assistant does not guess from the request; it asks the wearer to scan the desk and shelf slowly and to LookAt the tongs so the camera can read the band. Seeing the unpackaged bap and the clean tongs, the assistant injects the ordinary food-service rule, stated separately from the visible facts: bread that will be offered to visitors should be set out with a clean serving utensil rather than handled by hand. It first tells the wearer to clear the snack area by moving the folder onto the bedroom shelf. After the wearer grabs the folder and puts it on the shelf, the assistant confirms from the new view and says to put the bottle of water on the desk as the drink. When the water is placed, the assistant checks the desk and, applying the rule, tells the wearer to bring the clean tongs to the desk before the bap. Once the tongs are on the desk, the assistant gives the final step: put the bap on the desk beside the tongs and stop, leaving the tongs out. A weak guide would treat this as ordinary tidying and leave the tongs on the shelf. The scored final state has the folder on the bedroom shelf and the bottle of water, bap, and clean tongs on the desk.

reviews.reason: This is a valid GUIDE.DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE_INJECTION episode: the decisive rule (ready-to-eat food offered to visitors should be set out with a clean serving utensil rather than handled by hand) is external knowledge that appears nowhere in the room, and it is applied to visually established facts (an unpackaged bap and tongs whose cleanliness is encoded by a short 'CLEAN' band, not by category alone). The rule is separated from the visual facts, the hidden clean state is properly encoded, and label reading is not the main challenge. The strong and weak branches diverge on a scorable final relation (tongs on the desk vs left on the shelf), the assistant delivers guidance incrementally across an initial plus three state-grounded feedback turns, and the structure (co-locating a required accessory) is distinct from the existing segregation (96001) and storage-condition (97001) templates. All props bind to allowed categories, counts and surface capacities are within limits, and the path is executable within the action budget.
requirements: Keep the 'CLEAN' band to no more than 8 characters and ensure it is explicitly inspected via LookAt before the utensil rule is invoked.
Ensure the desk never exceeds its reference capacity of 3 (water + bap + tongs = 3 is the maximum).
Confirm each later assistant turn is preceded by an observed placement effect, not merely a new turn.
